title: Local contraction survives additive tensor pullback
statement: Let $p:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and assume its tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] is additive. Let $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ satisfy $\bigcup_i U_i=X$, and let $G$ be any $\mathcal O_X$-module. For the explicit augmentation $\epsilon:G[0]\to C$ [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction], both $\epsilon$ and $p^*(\operatorname{extend}\epsilon)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. There is no affineness, separatedness, quasi-coherence or flatness hypothesis.

proof.text: On U_i, insert i into an increasing tuple in its ordered position, with sign (-1) to that position; set the operator to zero for a repeated index. At degree zero project to the singleton i. In dh+hd the face deleting the inserted i gives the identity; each other deletion cancels against the same restriction composite with opposite sign. This contracts the augmented complex on U_i.

Tensor pullback commutes with restriction to the inverse-image opens. Apply its additivity to the local homotopy identities: it preserves sums, integer multiples, compositions and identities. Thus the pulled-back augmentation is locally a homotopy equivalence as well. Homology of module sheaves is local on the two covers, so both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Extension by zero adds only zero terms. For r=0 both schemes are empty.
